This role leads Microsoft 365 integrations, separations, and tenant migrations associated with mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and tenant consolidations. The Collaboration Solutions Engineer is responsible for planning and executing solutions that transition users, data, collaboration services, and configurations while maintaining business continuity, security, compliance, and a positive employee experience. This role will partner with business leaders and stakeholders, to translate transaction requirements into practical migration strategies and execution plans across the Microsoft product stack. This role offers the opportunity to influence enterprise-scale transactions and modernization initiatives across a diverse portfolio of businesses. Travel of up to 10% may be required. Occasional evening, after-hours, or weekend work may be necessary to support migration activities, cutovers, and stabilization efforts. The role requires the ability to work with confidential information and coordinate effectively across business units, vendors, and global stakeholders. We deliver IT products and services that enable employee success and collaboration. As a trusted partner, we focus on people, processes, technology, and data to drive transformation. Our team members are key contributors through the application of frameworks and principles with an emphasis on leveraging critical and economic thinking to drive value. Lead execution of Microsoft 365 migration solutions that enable secure, scalable movement of users, collaboration services, and business data between tenants using platforms such as Quest On Demand Migration and native Microsoft migration capabilities. Coordinate tenant-to-tenant migrations for Microsoft Entra ID identities and groups, Exchange Online mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint Online, Teams, and supported Power Platform or related workloads. Plan identity matching, target-account provisioning, UPN and SMTP changes, domain transfer activities, mail flow, calendar free/busy, Teams federation, and other coexistence requirements. Ensure successful migration outcomes through pilot execution, production cutovers, stakeholder coordination, issue resolution, validation activities, and post-migration stabilization. Create technical documentation, inventories, mapping files, risk and issue logs, test scripts, support knowledge, user communications, and operational handoff materials. Coordinate user acceptance testing, business validation, executive and stakeholder updates, service-desk readiness, training, and end-user communications to minimize disruption. Identify repeatable processes and use PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, APIs, reporting, and automation to improve migration quality, speed, traceability, and scale. Experience with tenant-to-tenant migration concepts, including identity mapping, coexistence, workload sequencing, data validation, cutover, and post-migration support. Ability to use or quickly learn migration platforms such as Quest On Demand Migration and native Microsoft cross-tenant migration capabilities. Experience using PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, APIs, CSV-based data analysis, or similar methods for discovery, bulk changes, validation, reporting, and troubleshooting. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical decisions, risks, and status to both technical and business audiences. Experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, tenant consolidations, carve-outs, or transition service agreement exit activities. Knowledge of Microsoft Exchange, Purview, Defender, Conditional Access, Intune, identity governance, data loss prevention, records management, and legal hold considerations. Experience with hybrid identity, Active Directory, device migration, external collaboration, domain cutovers, and enterprise change management. Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator Associate, Messaging Administrator Associate, Microsoft 365 Administrator Expert, or comparable migration-platform certifications. Ability to manage multiple workstreams, deadlines, risks, and stakeholders in projects with confidential information and transaction-driven timelines. At Koch companies, we are entrepreneurs. This means we openly challenge the status quo, find new ways to create value and get rewarded for our individual contributions. Our work spans a vast number of industries across the world, including engineered technology, refining, chemicals and polymers, pulp and paper, glass, electronics and many more. Headquartered in Wichita, Kansas, Koch employs about 120,000 employees across the globe. At Koch, employees are empowered to do what they do best to make life better. Learn how our business philosophy helps employees unleash their potential while creating value for themselves and the company. We provide essential resources and support to build and maintain physical, financial, and emotional strength - focusing on overall wellbeing so you can focus on what matters most. Our benefits plan includes - medical, dental, vision, flexible spending and health savings accounts, life insurance, ADD, disability, retirement, paid vacation/time off, educational assistance, and may also include infertility assistance, paid parental leave and adoption assistance. Specific eligibility criteria is set by the applicable Summary Plan Description, policy or guideline and benefits may vary by geographic region. We seek to enable the best work environment that helps you and the business work together to produce superior results. review_candidates.description: Description System Application Architect, you will define, scale, and secure connected-health ecosystem for Cardiac Rhythm Management (CRM). Operating as a senior individual contributor, this role bridges the end-to-end software spectrum – from on-device telemetry and embedded interfaces to streaming cloud infrastructure, big data pipelines, AI/ML enablement, and clinician/patient application platforms. Beyond core system design, you will serve as the cornerstone of technical thought leadership and governance across the organization. You will establish modern engineering guardrails, lead cross-functional architecture forums, and guide engineering teams through complex implementation cycles. Partnering closely with R&D, Product, Quality, Regulatory, and Security stakeholders, you will drive technology strategy to ensure our software ecosystem is secure, resilient, compliant, and directly aligned with long-term business growth. Requirements General expectation Knowledge of applicable Cybersecurity and Privacy standards and regulations (HIPAA, GDPR, etc.) Knowledge of applicable medical software standards and regulations (FDA guidelines) DHF process understanding Cloud/AWS, Infrastructure/Terraform/Kubernetes experience System Architecture experience Communication with cross regional team in US and CEE Actively contributing to architectural decisions around Platform, Embedded, Mobile apps, Cloud, APIs, backend services, and data flows, with a strong focus on performance, security, and reliability Working closely with engineers to review designs, unblock implementation, and ensure architectural decisions are executed correctly Working with short-term MVP and with longer-term architectural improvements Contributing to effort estimation, roadmap prep, and the commercial proposal for MVP delivery Required Qualifications Experience: 10+ years of progressive software engineering experience, with at least 4+ years serving in a Principal Architect, Lead Architect, or Systems Architect capacity for large-scale distributed systems. Domain Expertise: Proven track record architecting high-reliability, cloud-native platforms within the MedTech, Digital Health, Biotech, or IoT device sectors. Direct experience handling continuous sensor data or streaming telemetry is highly preferred. Leadership & Communication: Exceptional ability to articulate complex architectural concepts, trade-offs, and risks to both executive stakeholders and engineering teams without direct line authority. Interoperability: Deep experience with healthcare data exchange standards (HL7, FHIR) and electronic health record (EHR/EMR) integrations. Data Stack & AI/ML: Familiarity with modern data stack tools (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery) and MLOps platforms for model deployment and clinical decision support. Author technical white papers and design blueprints to drive consensus on long-term engineering strategies. Evangelize best practices in system scalability, data modeling, time-series data storage, and microservices architecture across the organization. Engineering Team Guidance & Mentorship Provide hands-on guidance, technical direction, and architectural oversight to cross-functional engineering teams during implementation. Deconstruct complex architectural visions into actionable technical roadmaps and design patterns that development teams can seamlessly execute. Conduct rigorous architecture and code reviews to ensure alignment with defined data models, engineering standards, and security postures. Mentor senior and staff engineers, cultivating a culture of high performance, continuous learning, and robust engineering discipline. Cloud Infrastructure & Platform Architecture Design and implement high-availability, fault-tolerant, and horizontally scalable cloud architectures capable of handling millions of concurrent streaming device connections. Define blueprints for microservices infrastructure, serverless computing, and infrastructure-as-code (IaC). Implement robust business continuity, disaster recovery, and data replication strategies across multiple geographical regions.
